newsitem.title: USA: Ford profits nearly double to $686 million.
newsitem.headline: Ford profits nearly double to $686 million.

text.p: Record third-quarter profits in its core U.S. operations nearly doubled Ford Motor Co.'s earnings in the period despite continued weakness in foreign markets, the automaker said Wednesday.
Ford earned $686 million, a 92 percent gain from the $357 million in profits it recorded a year ago.
Of the total profit, net income from Ford's U.S. automotive operations was a third-quarter record at $634 million, compared with $187 million a year ago.

However, the improved results in the U.S. market were offset by increased losses in other markets, where Ford's automotive operations lost $619 million, compared with a loss of $388 million last year.
The red ink flowed deepest in Ford's European operations, which lost $472 million, following a loss of $320 million in the 1995 period.
The automaker said the deficit reflected costs associated with launching new products, an adverse vehicle mix and weak volume, coupled with continued high marketing costs.

However, it said its European high-volume vehicle launches were largely completed and that it would focus on cost reductions. It added that new products, such as the recently launched Ka small car that will go on sale next month, will strengthen its European line-up.
In South America, Ford lost $226 million in the quarter, compared with a loss of $102 million in 1995. Most of the losses stem from Brazil.

"Improvements in our U.S. automotive operations continue," said Alex Trotman, chairman and chief executive officer. "Outside the U.S., results continue to reflect challenges in several key regions, particularly Europe and South America."
Ford's Financial Services Group posted record earnings of $671 million, up from $558 million in the 1995 period.
The results included a one-time gain of $76 million from the sale of assets of USL Capital. Without the one-time gain, profits from Financial Services still set a third-quarter record.
Ford Credit earned $299 million, down from $357 million in last year's third quarter. The decline reflects an increase in credit losses, consistent with the consumer finance industry.
The Associates, Ford's consumer finance unit, reported third-quarter earnings of $230 million, a record for any quarter. As the majority shareholder, Ford's share was $186 million.
Ford's third-quarter earnings, equal to 56 cents a share, came on revenues of $34 billion. That compared with $31.4 billion in revenues in the year-ago period, when profits equalled 27 cents a share.
The latest results were boosted by two one-time gains totalling $37 million and include a one-time charge of $39 million for early retirements for U.S. workers.
Trotman said the automaker expected to take additional charges of $300 million to $400 million for early retirement programmes in the fourth quarter.
Ford said it spent an average of $1,100 on retail incentives in the United States in the third quarter, up from $850 a year ago and $945 in the second quarter of 1996.
Trotman said Ford expects its automotive results to improve in the fourth quarter from the 1995 period.
"We expect sales volumes will be higher and margins will continue to improve," he said, adding: "There's still much to do."
Ford's stock was unchanged at $32.75 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
